_comment: SOURCE OF TRUTH for the Kinetic Scenes roadmap rendered at /kinetic-scenes/roadmap. Hand-maintained, and it lists OPEN work only: when a task is done, document it on its guide page under /kinetic-scenes/ and delete it from here (the 228 tasks of phases 1-29 were retired this way on 2026-11-20; the guide pages describe them). Update `extensionVersion` to the Studio version.

milestones.title: Phase 30 · Four new motion styles
milestones.goal: Four looks Kinetic Scenes does not have yet, added like the other 51 styles: a card on the start screen and in the style picker, a guide that tells the AI how to build the look, a docs page and a place in What's new. Each is written from scratch for Kinetic Scenes, so it stays editable on the timeline and works with your voice, captions and brand.

tasks.title: Study the open animation-skills collection
tasks.detail: Read a public, MIT-licensed collection of AI animation skills for technique only (how it times captions to a voice, builds a stick figure, stacks voxels and follows a route with the camera). Nothing is copied, and the styles named after other creators are left out.

tasks.title: Stick figure explainer
tasks.detail: A whiteboard-white stage where stick figures act the idea out: they walk on, point, shrug and react on the beat of the voice, with simple props and captions. Quick to make and easy to read, for explainers and story reels.

tasks.title: Voxel build
tasks.detail: A scene built from cubes, block by block: a house, a desk or a city rises as the voice talks, with a slow orbiting camera and soft daylight. A generic blocky look, with no game's name, characters or textures.

tasks.title: 3D map route
tasks.detail: A tilted 3D map where a route draws itself from start to finish while the camera follows it, with pins, place names and a distance or time counting down. Extends the 2D Transit map style for travel, delivery and "how far" stories.

tasks.title: "What if" 3D explainer
tasks.detail: A recipe on top of the Toy 3D look for the cartoon "what if" format: one question, a 3D world that plays out the answer step by step, and captions timed to the voice-over.

milestones.title: Phase 31 · More effects for talking-head reels
milestones.goal: Effects for videos where a person talks to the camera, the gaps left after comparing the Studio with a public effects pack for talking-head reels. Each is written from scratch as a preset or a ready-made piece, so it stays editable on the timeline, uses Follow the face and the cut-out person (graphics can sit behind the speaker), and passes Check scene. Phone and app pieces get a generic look, with no app's branding.

tasks.title: Study the talking-head effects pack
tasks.detail: Read a public, MIT-licensed pack of talking-head reel effects for ideas only (what each effect does and when it is used). Nothing is copied; many of its effects are already presets or pieces here (tier list, comment box, magazine cover, checklist, receipt, spotlight, title behind the person, before and after, colour grades, captions, pause trimming).

tasks.title: Split push
tasks.detail: A headline card, a screenshot or a B-roll clip slides in from the top and pushes the speaker into the lower half of the frame, then slides away and gives the frame back. For "here is what it does" lines and B-roll over a talking head.

tasks.title: Profile grid
tasks.detail: The speaker shrinks into the centre tile of a 3 × 3 grid of reel tiles while the other tiles pop in one by one with view counts; a wall version fills the background behind the speaker while a counter rolls up.

tasks.title: 3D card carousel
tasks.detail: Cards (reel covers, screenshots, products) spin around the speaker on a tilted 3D ring, passing behind the cut-out person on the far side.

tasks.title: Phone UI pieces
tasks.detail: Three ready-made pieces in a generic phone style: a follow button that is tapped and flips to "Following", toggle switches that turn on one line at a time, and notifications that stack up with a soft glow.

tasks.title: Stamp
tasks.detail: A rubber stamp slams down on a word or a picture with a little shake and an ink-bleed edge ("REJECTED", "APPROVED", "SOLD OUT"), with a thud from the sound library.

tasks.title: Freeze frame with a drawn arrow
tasks.detail: The footage freezes on a frame, a hand-drawn arrow and a short note draw themselves on to point at something, then the video plays on.

tasks.title: Match cut
tasks.detail: A different page, picture or headline cuts in on each spoken word while one word stays locked in the same place across all of them.

tasks.title: LED sign
tasks.detail: A dot-matrix LED sign types a line out behind the speaker while the room dims, each lit dot glowing.

tasks.title: Glass widgets
tasks.detail: Frosted-glass widgets (a stat tile, a progress ring, a calendar, a now-playing card) float in around the speaker's head and drift gently.

tasks.title: Halftone paper page
tasks.detail: A cream paper page with the speaker cut out in a corner in halftone dots, while their words build up at the top in serif type with the keywords in red.

tasks.title: Tape label
tasks.detail: A strip of tape with a short line on it is slapped on at a slant, as on a box or a chest.

tasks.title: Dot reveal
tasks.detail: The picture builds itself out of glowing dots, then snaps into focus.

tasks.title: Rain behind the person
tasks.detail: Keys, icons or small pictures fall with physics behind the cut-out speaker and pile up at the bottom.

tasks.title: Lock-on brackets
tasks.detail: Corner brackets snap onto the speaker's face and track it while the camera gently follows, with a small label.

milestones.title: Phase 32 · Better 3D
milestones.goal: Better and wider 3D for scenes. Agents already build models and shots in Blender through the AI Dev Kit (blender_model, blender_render) and put them in 3D layers; this phase makes those models better, reaches shapes that scripted modelling cannot (a shoe, a plant, a character), and lets you work in a live Blender window when you want to. Each tool is optional and is switched on in the AI Dev Kit's Tools section, planned with the kit.

tasks.title: Picture to 3D model (trial)
tasks.detail: Try LATO.2 (MIT code and weights), an open picture-to-mesh model, for shapes scripts cannot model: a photo or an AI picture becomes a mesh, Blender cleans it up (decimate, materials, GLB) and it lands in a 3D layer. It needs a CUDA graphics card with more memory than this machine's 6 GB, so the trial also tests its hosted demo and a rented GPU before deciding.

tasks.title: Path-traced stills
tasks.detail: Render a 3D scene's still frame (the poster and the thumbnail) with a path tracer in Blender (Cycles) for soft shadows and real reflections, while the moving scene stays live on the page.

tasks.title: Screencasts of phone apps
tasks.detail: Record real Android apps for product tours and client reels: mirror and record an Android phone over USB with scrcpy (the Android Studio emulator when no phone is at hand), and bring the recording in as footage with the screencast tools. iPhone apps: the phone's own screen recording or mirroring it to the computer, since the iOS Simulator runs only on a Mac. The tools themselves are switched on in the AI Dev Kit's Tools section.

milestones.title: Still open from earlier phases
milestones.goal: The few tasks left from phases 1-29. Everything else from those phases is built and described on the guide pages.

tasks.title: Load media near the playhead
tasks.detail: Live scenes fetch each part's pictures and footage as the playhead nears it (the opening first, then ahead), showing the poster frame until then, instead of loading everything when the page opens. Needs a new player version and the Kinetic Scene element to use it.

tasks.title: Benchmark against hand-made videos
tasks.detail: Rebuild reference motion-graphics videos from their voice-overs with the new tools and compare them frame by frame, the way the Site Converter is measured against its sources, until the Studio's version holds up next to them. Round 1 rebuilt a 10-second side-by-side race explainer from the new pieces and fixed what it found (pills sized to their words, Change text resizing them smoothly); round 2 compares it frame by frame with the reference. Round 2 waits for the reference video.

tasks.title: Paste a link
tasks.detail: Paste a video link to make one like it, or to learn its rhythm only. The source is studied and then deleted, never reused, and captions are read first.

tasks.title: Watch a video
tasks.detail: A video_watch tool for agents, with a frame budget, a focus range and frames pinned to cues.

milestones.title: Later, only if people ask
milestones.goal: Cloud options that wait until people ask for projects across computers. Until then, projects stay in the browser and as folders on your computer.

tasks.title: Save to Google Drive
tasks.detail: Projects on any computer without our own server: people sign in with Google and their scenes are saved to their own Drive. Planned if people ask for cross-device projects. Needs a Google OAuth client ID from the site owner before it can be built. Deferred (2026-10-29): not planned until people ask for it; projects stay in the browser and as files.

tasks.title: Accounts and cloud projects (only if needed)
tasks.detail: If real accounts are ever needed (a project library, short links, embeds that update in place), they run on a free cloud tier, separate from the website hosting, with uploads on object storage and embeds still served from GitHub Pages. Deferred (2026-10-29): not planned until people ask for it; projects stay in the browser and as files.
